queries: WITH per_invoice AS (SELECT i.invoice_number, AVG(li.derived_product_cost) AS avg_product_cost, SUM(CASE WHEN li.derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND li.product_price IS NOT NULL THEN li.derived_total_cost END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN li.derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND li.product_price IS NOT NULL THEN li.product_price END), 0) AS ratio FROM Invoices i LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items li ON li.invoice_number = i.invoice_number GROUP BY i.invoice_number), overall AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM per_invoice) SELECT AVG(p.avg_product_cost) AS avg_product_cost, AVG(p.ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - o.avg_ratio) AS avg_amount_above_overall FROM per_invoice p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.ratio > o.avg_ratio

WITH invoice_metrics AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(derived_product_cost) AS avg_product_cost, 1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND product_price IS NOT NULL THEN derived_total_cost END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND product_price IS NOT NULL THEN product_price END), 0) AS ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), overall AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM invoice_metrics) SELECT AVG(im.avg_product_cost) AS average_product_cost, AVG(im.ratio) AS average_ratio, AVG(im.ratio - o.avg_ratio) AS average_excess_ratio FROM invoice_metrics AS im CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE im.ratio > o.avg_ratio

WITH invoice_stats AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(derived_product_cost) AS avg_product_cost, AVG(derived_total_cost / NULLIF(product_price, 0)) AS invoice_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(invoice_ratio) AS overall_ratio FROM invoice_stats) SELECT AVG(avg_product_cost) AS avg_product_cost, AVG(invoice_ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(invoice_ratio - overall_ratio) AS avg_amount_above_overall FROM invoice_stats CROSS JOIN baseline WHERE invoice_ratio > overall_ratio

assumptions.assumption: An invoice’s ratio is the sum of its available line total costs divided by the sum of the corresponding unit prices. An invoice with a zero denominator has no ratio.

alternatives.interpretation: An invoice’s ratio is the average of its individual line total-cost-to-unit-price ratios.

alternatives.interpretation: An invoice’s ratio is the average of its individual line ratios.

assumptions.assumption: An invoice’s ratio is the average of its line-level total-cost-to-unit-price ratios. Missing values and zero unit prices contribute no line-level ratio.

alternatives.interpretation: Calculate each invoice’s ratio by dividing its summed line total costs by its summed unit prices, using only lines where both values are present.
